TiN did not dissolve up to 1.8 V. In 0.1 M NaCl, pitting corrosion initiated at approximately 0.37 V and 0.61 V in the MnS- and TiS 2 -added specimens, respectively, indicating that dissolution of MnS and (Mn,Ti)S triggered pit initiation in the respective specimens. In commercial Fe–16Cr stainless steel, the inclusions were identified as MnS. In arc-melted Fe–16Cr–0.17Ti, they included Ti-containing oxides, TiN, and TiS. The average pitting potentials were 0.38 V for Fe–16Cr and 0.51 V for Fe–16Cr–0.17Ti. Because inclusion dissolution induces pit initiation, MnS and (Mn,Ti)S were expected to be the respective pit-initiation sites in Fe–16Cr and Fe–16Cr–0.17Ti, although electron microscopy and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy did not reveal (Mn,Ti)S. Galvanostatic polarization in 0.1 M NaCl produced pits several micrometers in diameter. MnS remained at the pit-initiation sites in Fe–16Cr, whereas Mn and S were detected at the pit-initiation sites in Fe–16Cr–0.17Ti. These findings verify the predicted pit-initiation sites.

title: Water vapor retards grain growth during sintering of yttria-stabilized zirconia pellets and coatings
abstract: Yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ) is the benchmark thermal barrier topcoat, but its sintering response to water vapor is unclear. YSZ pellets of three initial porosities and free-standing plasma-sprayed coatings were heat-treated at 1300 °C in dry air, steam, or dry nitrogen. Contrary to reported promotion in simple oxides, steam retarded microstructural evolution. After 100 h the most porous pellet showed a 31% smaller grain size in steam, with apparent rate constants lower by factors of 2.8–4.2. A dry-nitrogen control in the same furnace changed the grain size by only 5.5%, isolating water vapor. Coatings likewise retained higher porosity and, at intermediate exposures, lower thermal conductivity. DFT calculations showed preferential OH binding at a grain-boundary Y 3+ site (−2.73 eV); a defect-equilibrium sensitivity analysis predicted 8–22% oxygen-vacancy depletion. These results support a mechanism in which OH-mediated grain-boundary stabilization through Y 3+ anchoring and vacancy-related defect modification leads to the retardation of sintering.

title: A study on the compatibility and service life of aluminium capacitors and synthetic coolants
abstract: Driven by surging power densities in data centres, immersion cooling is critical for high-heat-flux dissipation. However, despite their widespread use in data centres, there remains a lack of research into the compatibility of surface-mount aluminium electrolytic capacitors with coolants. This study evaluates the reliability of conductive polymer capacitors in synthetic oil through accelerated ageing tests at 70 °C, 80 °C, and 100 °C. Results identify butyl rubber swelling as the primary failure mode, causing structural deformation that precludes circuit assembly, rather than electrical drift. This degradation is driven by coolant molecules infiltrating the rubber matrix, inducing chain extension and reduced thermal stability. Simultaneously, poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) (PEDOT) de-doping increases the equivalent series resistance. Based on the Arrhenius model, the swelling-induced failure yields an activation energy of 43.7 kJ/mol, predicting a time to structural failure of approximately 492 days at 50 °C. These findings elucidate the physicochemical interactions between components and coolants, providing a theoretical framework for reliability design in immersion-cooled systems.

title: Triggering biodegradation of PLA and PBAT blend films by microembossing
abstract: In the present work, mechanical embossing with microstamps is used to support biodegradation of PLA/PBAT blends. Films of PLA/PBAT are modified by a microembossing process, using metallic stamps with different surfaces. Subsequently, biodegradation is carried out by incubation with Bacillus subtilis DSM 10. The biodegradation efficiency is evaluated through comparative LSM, WLI, mass loss measurements, as well as ATR-FTIR, Raman microscopy, XRD, REM, DSC and EDX before and after the bioegradation process. Results show that the structuring process leads to a significant increase in the degradation rate of the investigated PLA/PBAT blend. The results can be explained by a relative enrichment of PBAT in the near-surface region after degradation, indicating that the PLA component is preferentially degraded through enzymatic cleavage and subsequent microbial metabolization. The findings further demonstrate that the structure-modified surface enables a deliberately tunable PLA/PBAT film interaction with water: the surface exhibits hydrophobic static wettability alongside a controllable pinning effect during use, while a marked improvement in biodegradation is achieved when brought in contact with microorganisms. Mechanical structuring thus represents a simple, chemical-free, and industrially scalable approach to controlling this dual behavior.

title: Detecting the onset and progression of spinodal decomposition using transient grating spectroscopy
abstract: Spinodal decomposition can degrade corrosion resistance and embrittle materials. The ability to quickly, non-destructively detect spinodal decomposition via elastic property measurements before catastrophic materials degradation would represent a significant advance in materials testing. We demonstrate that spinodal decomposition can be detected in a binary Fe-Cr alloy via modulus stiffening using ex situ (and in situ) transient grating spectroscopy (TGS). The modulus stiffening is attributable to the convex dependence of the \(C{\prime}\) elastic modulus on chromium content within certain compositional limits, which has been established by prior density functional theory studies. Over this range of initial chromium compositions, chromium partitioning due to spinodal decomposition raises the average \(C{\prime}\) modulus such that the decomposed Fe-Cr alloy is stiffer than the initial solid solution. The presence and extent of spinodal decomposition in a 36 at. % chromium alloy are confirmed using atom probe tomography (APT), and are consistent with atomistic simulations that predict elastic modulus stiffening in the same alloy. The observed spinodal decomposition via APT is used to predict an expected modulus stiffening which, based on a simple model, agrees in sign and order of magnitude with the observed stiffening via TGS. The quantitative link between an observed composition change and a measured elastic response suggests TGS as a potential tool for non-destructive evaluation of spinodal decomposition in high-chromium ferritic phases in steels.

title: Oxygen-mediated phase evolution and elemental partitioning in a Ni-based superalloy during thermal-mechanical-chemical erosion
abstract: Phase evolution and elemental partitioning behavior of the GH4098 Ni-based superalloy were investigated in detail using multi-scale electron-microscopy-based analytical techniques after repeated testing cycles of thermal–chemical–mechanical erosion in a vented combustor. Localized melting and redeposition of molten materials have been confirmed, with the maximum temperature at the bore surface exceeding the melting point during transient thermal cycles upon exposure to high-temperature propellant gas. The major phase constituents in the redeposited materials evolve from Cr-containing oxides on a γ-matrix to partitioned clusters of Cr/Al-rich oxides, Ni–Co–Fe solid-solution, and Ti–Mo intermetallic phases during repeated oxidation processes, and finally to a continuous Cr–Al–Ti-containing oxide region enclosing isolated metallic domains. The results of first-principles calculations further reveal that Cr-rich oxides are preferentially formed due to a low energy barrier and low adsorption energy for O atoms on localized regions enriched with Cr. Segregation of W at the interface of Cr-rich oxides also takes place through energetically favored paths for migration. In addition, the formation of Ti–Mo intermetallic phases is preferred upon intermediate contents of interstitial O atoms, while the partitioning of major alloying elements including Ni, Co and Fe leads to the presence of solid-solution phases.

title: Interaction effects between fungi and hydrogel antifungal coating under microgravity-induced diffusion limitation
abstract: The long-term performance of antifungal coatings in microgravity is critical for spacecraft applications, yet how altered mass transport regulates fungus–coating interactions and coating degradation remains unclear. Here, a hydrogel antifungal coating (SDM) on aluminium alloy coupons was evaluated against Aspergillus brasiliensis during a 90-day parallel experiment conducted aboard the China Space Station (CSS) and under ground conditions. We reveal that microgravity-induced diffusion limitation does not simply enhance or suppress antifungal performance but reshapes fungus–coating interfacial interactions. Restricted transport reduced fungal colonisation, while incomplete hydration-layer formation under microgravity resulted in a lower anti-biofilm adhesion rate (52.83%) than that under ground conditions (57.44%). Meanwhile, fungal stress adaptation increased organic acid production, but limited interfacial transport reduced the accumulation and action of corrosive metabolites, mitigating coating degradation. Consistent with this mechanism, chemical structure analysis showed attenuated carbonyl-related degradation signals in space-exposed coatings, whereas ground coupons exhibited more pronounced structural deterioration. These findings reveal a diffusion-controlled mechanism governing the antifungal and degradation behaviour of functional coatings under microgravity.

title: Corrosion analysis of bare and open-air plasma-assisted organosilicon-coated aluminum alloy 7075 using electrochemical polarization
abstract: A novel open-air plasma jet process was used to deposit organosilicon corrosion barrier coating on aluminum alloy 7075-T6 (Al 7075); its protection effect was evaluated by electrochemical polarization and ASTM B117 salt spray exposure tests. Three independent processes (P/a, P/b, and P/c conditions) produced continuous and dense coating with representative thicknesses of approximately 780, 1380, and 1630 nm, respectively, and similar Si, O, and C contents in the examined STEM-EDS regions. To set a reasonable basis for electrochemical corrosion evaluation, a localized corrosion stabilization potential of uncoated Al 7075 was investigated by analyzing current transients at different anodic overpotentials in 3.5% NaCl, revealing a marginal passive regime of <54 mV for Al 7075. Under a 60 mV anodic overpotential, the approximately 1630 nm P/c-coated specimens maintained low currents in all four tests, suggesting corrosion-protection performance that may be comparable to the approximately 19 µm anodized condition within the limited dataset in the present testing conditions. In the ASTM B117 exposure tests conducted only for the uncoated and down-selected P/c-coated Al 7075, the organosilicon layer exhibited only minor corrosion damage compared to the uncoated Al 7075 that suffered from severe corrosion attack after 962 h. This work reports a novel corrosion barrier coating and a method for determining the localized corrosion stabilization potential of Al 7075.

title: Pack cementation coatings for degradation control of refractory high entropy alloys
abstract: Refractory high-entropy alloys offer high-temperature strength but degrade rapidly in oxidizing environments. This Review examines halide-activated pack cementation as a surface-design strategy for controlling oxidation-driven degradation. We connect coating growth, silicide and aluminide formation, protective-scale chemistry and failure modes, and propose design criteria for coating architectures that retain protective reservoirs while avoiding brittle reaction zones.

title: Effect of Cr-rich precipitates on the wear and corrosion resistance of FeNiCoCr multi-principal element alloy coatings
abstract: Marine engineering structures are simultaneously exposed to chloride-rich corrosive atmospheres and mechanical wear. Although multi-principal element alloy (MPEA) coatings are attractive protective candidates, combining high wear resistance with long-term corrosion stability remains challenging. Here, three non-equiatomic FeNiCoCr MPEA coatings with distinct distributions of Cr-rich precipitates are comparatively investigated by dry sliding tests and 60-day acetic acid salt spray exposure. The Fe 5 Ni 2 Co 2 Cr coating, containing discrete nanoscale Cr-rich precipitates, exhibits the lowest wear rate (approximately 2.0 × 10 −5 mm 3 N −1 m −1 ) and only isolated shallow pits after 60 days, with its surface evolving towards a Cr-rich, Fe-lean near-surface layer. In contrast, an interconnected precipitate network provides brittle intergranular paths for wear-induced delamination and Cr-lean anodic paths for localized corrosion. Controlling precipitate continuity and Cr distribution is therefore an effective microstructural design strategy for durable MPEA coatings in marine environments.
